organisations.name: Rathmore Health Research CLG
organisations.description: An independent, non-profit health-research organisation based in Dublin with 18 employees. Its principal activity is conducting human-health research. It designed the REST-Ireland study, chooses the research question, participant eligibility, collected fields, analysis plan, publication and retention periods, and recruits volunteers directly from the Irish community. It does not provide clinical care, operate health insurance or a clearinghouse, submit insurance claims or eligibility transactions, or perform services for US healthcare providers or health plans. It has no US establishment. The study is funded from its own unrestricted reserves, with no external funder or commercial sponsor.

organisations.name: Hudson Quay Analytics Inc.
organisations.description: A for-profit statistical-computing company with 26 employees, headquartered in Brooklyn, New York. It provides managed analysis workspaces for independent European research organisations. For REST-Ireland it will host the coded study records and run Rathmore's specified statistical scripts solely on Rathmore's documented instructions. It does not select the research aims, recruit or contact participants, determine new uses, or reuse records for advertising, product development or model training. It does not diagnose or treat people, operate a health plan or healthcare clearinghouse, conduct healthcare insurance transactions, or serve US healthcare providers, health plans, business associates or their subcontractors. Its staff, company-operated servers and backups for this project are all in New York State. No external hosting, support or analysis subcontractor is involved.

transfer.title: REST-Ireland: Dublin research organisation commissions coded-data analysis in New York

data.description: A research dataset for 3,600 consenting adults resident in Ireland: a randomly generated study code, ten-year age band, broad Irish province, study-week number, self-reported sleep-duration band, fatigue score, pain-interference score and a yes/no indicator of sleep-medication use. No name, contact details, exact date of birth, address, employer, clinical-record identifier, precise location, free text, genetic data or biometric identifiers are exported. Rathmore alone holds the separate participant-to-code correspondence table in Ireland. Hudson Quay receives neither that table nor credentials or means to access it. These are participant-supplied research measurements, not records obtained from a hospital, insurer or US healthcare organisation.

transfer.purpose_description: REST-Ireland is a specified twelve-week observational study of associations between sleep patterns, fatigue and pain interference in adults. Rathmore owns the protocol and analysis plan and intends to publish disclosure-checked aggregate findings. Hudson Quay provides computing and instructed statistical execution, not an independent research project. The study provides no diagnosis, treatment recommendation, clinical score or automated decision about an individual.
transfer.necessity: The repeated study code connects the same volunteer's weekly measurements and permits Rathmore to correct records or remove a withdrawing participant before final anonymised outputs are produced. Fully unlinked records would not support the planned longitudinal analysis or that withdrawal handling. The correspondence table and direct identifiers are unnecessary for Hudson Quay's work and remain in Ireland. Each exported field is justified in the approved analysis plan. Hudson Quay was selected for its validated longitudinal-analysis environment; no claim is made that a US location is essential or that consent alone permits a third-country transfer.
transfer.retention: Weekly exports start on 19 October 2026 and stop after the twelve-week collection period. Hudson Quay retains the coded workspace only until analysis sign-off, no later than 30 June 2027, then deletes active copies within 7 days and backups within 30 days. Earlier withdrawals are removed from the active workspace within 7 days and from backups within 30 days. Rathmore keeps its study working records under the same analysis timetable, then retains only anonymised aggregate results. Its separate consent and governance records remain in Ireland for five years under the documented schedule and are never supplied to Hudson Quay.
transfer.onward: No other recipient, subprocessor, affiliate or external analyst receives or can access participant-level records. Five authorised Hudson Quay analysts and two administrators are the only US personnel permitted access; access is confined to this instructed workspace. Rathmore receives the analysis outputs. Only anonymised aggregate findings, with small-cell suppression and disclosure review, may be published. There is no return of data to a US hospital, insurer, employer or commercial sponsor.
transfer.method: Rathmore sends allow-listed export files through an authenticated TLS connection to a segregated workspace on Hudson Quay's company-operated New York servers. Storage and backups are encrypted, accounts are named and use MFA, exports are logged, and local analyst downloads are disabled. Hudson Quay's authorised administrators can technically decrypt its coded workspace; encryption is not presented as preventing all recipient access or as making the records anonymous.
transfer.additional_info: This is a new study. Health-data collection starts on 12 October 2026 and the first US export is proposed for 19 October 2026; neither has begun. All 3,600 enrolled participants are adults who opted in before collection. They are recruited independently of employers or healthcare services, receive no treatment through the study, and can refuse or withdraw without disadvantage. The proposed purpose, fields, recipient, access and deletion periods are the same in the consent material, ethics approval, processing agreement and study protocol. The supplied evidence includes original document summaries and named declarations about existing controls. Full copies of the DPIA, detailed security test reports and both organisations' processing registers are not attached; their completion and project scope are addressed by the named declarations. The first quarterly governance review is scheduled for 15 January 2027 and its report does not yet exist.

evidence.title: REST-Ireland participant information sheet and explicit-consent register, version 2.1
evidence.summary: The register records a dated, freely given, specific and explicit affirmative opt-in from each of the 3,600 adults before any study health-data collection. The information sheet describes the specified sleep, fatigue and pain study, the listed health measurements, Rathmore's collection and research use, Hudson Quay Analytics Inc.'s instructed hosting and analysis in New York, the separate Ireland-held lookup table, retention and rights. The health-data consent is distinct from general terms and is not bundled with unrelated purposes. There is no employment, care-access, payment or service condition; refusal has no disadvantage. Withdrawal uses the same simple study-office channel as enrolment, stops further collection and exports, and triggers the stated removal process before final anonymised outputs. It explains that already published anonymised aggregates cannot identify or be removed for an individual. No broad future-research, advertising or training consent is taken. The sheet separately explains the DPF transfer arrangement; participant consent is not offered as an Article 49 transfer derogation.

evidence.title: Executed REST-Ireland data-processing and statistical-services agreement
evidence.summary: Signed by Rathmore and Hudson Quay for this exact study and workspace, effective before collection and export. Describes the subject matter, duration, instructed operations, health-data fields, adult participants and Rathmore's rights. Hudson Quay processes only documented instructions, binds authorised personnel to confidentiality, implements the agreed safeguards, assists with rights requests, incidents and impact assessments, supports audits and returns or deletes records on instruction. It must notify Rathmore of an instruction it considers unlawful. Independent reuse, participant contact and model training are prohibited. No subprocessors are authorised; adding one would require Rathmore's prior written approval and an amended assessment. The agreement applies to the New York servers, analysis staff and administrators, not merely to an affiliate or another product.

evidence.title: Active EU-US Data Privacy Framework listing and scope extract for Hudson Quay Analytics Inc.
evidence.summary: The supplied listing names the exact receiving legal entity, Hudson Quay Analytics Inc., as an active EU-US DPF participant subject to Federal Trade Commission jurisdiction. Its non-HR personal-data coverage includes sensitive health-research data received for instructed hosting and statistical services, including this New York workspace and its authorised staff. It covers the recipient itself, not a parent or affiliate. The listing and applicable privacy notice were checked on 7 October 2026; the certification is current through 14 September 2027, beyond the stated US processing and deletion period. No UK-only or Swiss-only entry is substituted for EU-US participation. The study's explicit opt-in covers the sensitive health-data use. The contract requires prompt notice of any change to participation or coverage and suspension of new exports if the stated transfer arrangement ceases to cover the service.

evidence.title: DPO declaration of completed REST-Ireland DPIA and launch assessment
evidence.summary: Niamh Keane confirms that the final DPIA was completed and approved on 30 September 2026, before collection or export, and covers Rathmore's full study plus Hudson Quay's New York storage, staff access, statistical execution, backups and deletion. It assesses the 3,600-person repeated health-data collection, consent and withdrawal, reidentification and confidentiality risks, the separate lookup table, international access, data minimisation and participant rights. It records consultation with the research team and recipient security lead, the specified controls and residual-risk acceptance, with no unmitigated high risk requiring prior consultation identified. It records no children, biometric identification, clinical monitoring of public areas or automated decisions with significant individual effects. This declaration concerns a completed assessment for the current protocol, not an intention to complete it after launch. The full DPIA is retained by Rathmore but is not attached to this submission.
evidence.attested_by: Niamh Keane, Data Protection Officer, Rathmore Health Research CLG

evidence.title: Rathmore Research Ethics Committee approval REC-2026-041
evidence.summary: Final approval dated 21 September 2026 for REST-Ireland protocol 2.1, its participant sheet, explicit opt-in, fields, withdrawal handling and the named New York analysis arrangement. The committee is established by Rathmore, whose principal activity is health research; its membership includes independent external ethics and lay members, with the principal investigator excluded from the approval vote. The letter records consideration of scientific benefit, methodology, consent, privacy, researcher competence, risks and independence from funders. It contains no outstanding pre-start conditions. Rathmore is the study sponsor and sole purpose-setting research organisation; Hudson Quay's instructed processing is identified in the approved protocol. No consent waiver or Health Research Consent Declaration Committee declaration is sought or granted.

evidence.title: REST-Ireland approved protocol, governance and research-safeguards procedure
evidence.summary: Protocol 2.1 specifies Rathmore's research responsibility, Hudson Quay's instructed operations, own-reserves funding, the ethics approval, and no other record-level recipient or external supporter. Collection is limited to consented adults and the justified fields; staff have completed role-specific data-protection and study training before access. Rathmore separates direct identifiers and the correspondence table in Ireland, restricts that table to its authorised study coordinators, and sends only the coded export. The procedure specifies access approval, logs, correction and withdrawal propagation, incident response, periodic control evaluation, retention, destruction and disclosure review. The longitudinal working dataset retains codes only while repeated measures and participant withdrawal require them. Final publications use anonymised aggregates with cell sizes below 15 suppressed and no participant-level release. The first quarterly review on 15 January 2027 is a scheduled monitoring activity, not an outstanding approval to start the study.

evidence.title: Joint declaration of operational REST-Ireland security and deletion controls
evidence.summary: Niamh Keane and Daniel Mercer confirm that the agreed safeguards are operational at both organisations for this specific study. These include authenticated encrypted transfer, encryption at rest and in backups, named MFA accounts, least-privilege permissions, separate Ireland-only access to the correspondence table, disabled local analyst downloads, access and export logging, incident escalation and approved support tickets. Hudson Quay's own staff operate the servers and backups in New York; no outside host or support vendor has access. Restore and deletion tests were completed on a synthetic test dataset in September 2026, with the stated active-copy and backup expiry periods verified. Personnel confidentiality undertakings and training were completed before access was authorised. Detailed test reports are retained internally and are not attached; this is a declaration of completed tests and existing controls, not a proposed security plan.
evidence.attested_by: Niamh Keane, Data Protection Officer, Rathmore Health Research CLG; Daniel Mercer, Chief Security Officer, Hudson Quay Analytics Inc.

evidence.title: REST-Ireland participant privacy notice and rights-handling procedure
evidence.summary: Delivered to participants before enrolment and health-data collection. Names Rathmore and its DPO, the specified research purpose and explicit-consent basis, the fields, the exact Hudson Quay recipient, US storage and access, DPF reliance and how to obtain its scope information, retention, consent withdrawal, access, correction, erasure and complaint rights. Gives the Irish Data Protection Commission complaint route and the study-office contact. States that participation is voluntary, there is no automated individual decision, and Hudson Quay cannot use the records for its own purposes. Rathmore handles rights requests using its Ireland-held code table; Hudson Quay must locate, restrict, correct or delete the matching coded records on Rathmore's instruction. Consent and governance documents kept in Ireland have their separate stated retention period.

evidence.title: Joint declaration of current controller and processor processing records
evidence.summary: Niamh Keane confirms that Rathmore's current processing record identifies REST-Ireland, its consent-based purpose, participants and health-data fields, Hudson Quay, US transfers and DPF coverage, rights handling, retention and safeguards. Maya Ortiz separately confirms that Hudson Quay maintains its own record of the processing categories carried out for Rathmore, including the New York hosting and statistical operations, recipient and exporter contacts, US location and transfer information, and technical and organisational safeguards. Both records were updated and reviewed for protocol 2.1 before launch; the statement does not rely solely on Rathmore's record to establish Hudson Quay's separate record. The registers are retained by their respective organisations and are not attached to this submission.
evidence.attested_by: Niamh Keane, Data Protection Officer, Rathmore Health Research CLG; Maya Ortiz, Privacy Lead, Hudson Quay Analytics Inc.

evidence.title: Approved REST-Ireland export specification and pre-launch validation record
evidence.summary: Version 2.1 permits exactly the coded fields listed in this request and no free text or direct identifiers. The code is randomly generated and is not derived from a name or national identifier. Rathmore alone holds the correspondence table. A synthetic dry run verified the allow-list, encrypted connection, receipt logging, disabled local downloads and withdrawal-by-code workflow. The source is participants' study questionnaires, with no hospital or payer record import. The validation relates to the named Hudson Quay workspace and does not claim that coded records have become anonymous or that encryption removes the need for a transfer arrangement.

expected.policy_context: v15 input; evidence-presence, as-described and closed-corpus policies; scenario authored on 8 October 2026 before the proposed architecture fixes
look_for: Infer Rathmore's purpose-setting/controller role and Hudson Quay's instructed/processor role from facts and the executed agreement, without treating either role as a declared input field.

Exclude HIPAA using the parties' activities and absence of any covered-entity/business-associate relationship. A US company handling health-related research data does not by itself engage HIPAA. Do not mistake the New York location or the word health for a US healthcare-provider nexus.
Treat the coded dataset as personal health data because Rathmore holds the correspondence table. Direct-identifier removal and encryption are safeguards, not a claim of anonymity.

Screen Article 6 consent and Article 9 explicit-consent routes for the specified research and instructed processing. Do not require a healthcare/professional-secrecy route for this non-treatment study merely because the records concern health.

Recognise an actual EEA-to-US transfer and assess the supplied exact-entity, current, non-HR and sensitive-data DPF coverage. Do not treat consent to processing as Article 49 transfer consent or US adequacy as unconditional for every company.

Investigate the Irish health-research rules and their amendments where needed. Explicit participant consent, qualifying ethics approval and the stated governance/safeguards are supplied. Distinguish these safeguards from the separate GDPR lawful basis and special-category condition. No consent declaration or legacy-study exception is needed merely because this is research.

Apply the evidence-presence policy consistently to the three named declarations. They address completed DPIA work, existing security and both parties' processing records; absence of the full internal reports or registers is not, under this prototype policy, proof of failure or an unanswered completion predicate.

Use evidence only within its stated party and activity scope. The DPF entry concerns the actual US recipient; the ethics letter concerns Rathmore's study; the joint declarations expressly cover the named parties rather than relying on a sender-only attestation.

Keep future quarterly governance review and verification of continuing controls/DPF coverage as proportionate monitoring or confirmations. Do not convert a report that is not yet due into a failed pre-launch gate.

Complete a valid supervisor finish with each current finding accepted. If a material interpretation remains disputed, name the exact actor, operation and predicate instead of returning an unexplained review-budget fallback.
acceptable_variations: A well-supported not_applicable DPIA finding is acceptable if the model concludes no mandatory DPIA trigger applies while recognising the supplied completed assessment; cohort size alone is not stipulated to prove large-scale processing.

Proceed is acceptable if the assessment finds every relevant gate supported and genuinely has no remaining confirmations. Do not invent a condition solely to reproduce the preferred proceed_subject_to_conditions label.
HIPAA may be excluded before dispatch; a supported supervisor exclusion is equivalent to a not_applicable HIPAA finding.

Expected statuses are pre-run hypotheses under the stated prototype policies, not binding answers or proof that any consent form, attestation or certificate would satisfy every real-world requirement.

expected.note: Synthetic case-study candidate. Both organisations, all named personnel, the study, documents, approvals, declarations and DPF listing are invented. Realistic names are used for readability; no claim is made about an actual organisation, person, certification or participant. The request contains narrative descriptions and an aggregate cohort count, not individual patient records. Expected metadata is for evaluation only, stays outside request and is not sent to the agents. No live outcome has been established.
